statements.new_statement_en: The state should lower barriers to imports and new competitors, even if existing local businesses lose income.

split.plus_en: Fewer barriers for imports and new competitors in concentrated consumer markets (food, banking, pharmacies, transport, car services, media, insurance)
split.minus_en: Protection of incumbent firms and local producers from imports and new entrants
split.statement_en: The state should lower barriers to imports and new competitors, even if existing local businesses lose income.

split.plus_en: Open, equal tenders for all suppliers in government purchasing
split.minus_en: Preference or tender exemptions for Israeli-made goods and for suppliers from priority regions (Negev, periphery, confrontation lines)
split.statement_en: When the government buys goods and services, it should prefer Israeli and local suppliers, even if it pays more.

reason: The heavy bills fall into two different issues. (A) Competition in consumer markets: food-sector competition law and parallel imports, mortgage switching and early-repayment fees, foreign financial licences, pharmacies outside HMO arrangements, ride-sharing, car services, broadcasting market (#1-2): about 75% of the weight, all 'toward'. The current q42 fits them, but the price 'local producers' only fits imports; 'existing local businesses' also covers banks, taxis and broadcasters. Caveat: #1-2 (digital broadcasting temporary order, Second Authority amendment 50) carry ~100 weight mostly from votes; voters may see them as media-politics laws rather than competition laws, so the customer should check that label. (B) Government procurement: Buy Israeli in wartime, local defence production, preference for Negev, periphery and confrontation-line suppliers, tender exemptions (#6,10,13,26,31,32,38), all 'away'. This is a separate voter question (should the state pay more to buy local), and q42 does not ask it. Left out: #5 Basic Law on reserve service (reservists' rights in general, procurement only incidental), #17 and #39 (land allocation), #18/19/35 (consumer cancellation rights, not competition), #22 (tender exemption for food-rescue charities, a welfare issue). The new B statement takes key '-' to balance the '+' of A.
